PEDANTICAL: Of or pertaining to a pedant; characteristic of, or resembling, a pedant; ostentatious of learning; as, a pedantic writer; a pedantic description; a pedantical affectation. "Figures pedantical." Shak.
POMPON: 1. Any trifling ornament for a woman's dress or bonnet. 2. (Mil.) A tuft or ball of wool, or the like, sometimes worn by soldiers on the front of the hat, instead of a feather.
PALPIGER: That portion of the labium which bears the palpi in insects.
PRINCELY: 1. Of or relating to a prince; regal; royal; of highest rank or authority; as, princely birth, character, fortune, etc. 2. Suitable for, or becoming to, a prince; grand; august; munificent; magnificent; as, princely virtues; a princely fortune. "Most princely gifts." Shak. In a princely manner. My appetite was not princely got. Shak.
PANISLAMISM: A desire or plan for the union of all Mohammedan nations for the conquest of the world.
PODAGRICAL: 1. Pertaining to the gout; gouty; caused by gout. 2. Afflicted with gout. Sir T. Browne.
PYTHIAN: Of or pertaining to Delphi, to the temple of Apollo, or to the priestess of Apollo, who delivered oracles at Delphi. Pythian games (Gr. Antiq.), one of the four great national festivals of ancient Greece, celebrated near Delphi, in honor of Apollo, the conqueror of the dragon Python, at first once in eight years, afterward once in four.
POTARGO: A kind of sauce or pickle. King.
PUPAL: Of or pertaining to a pupa, or the condition of a pupa.
PRE-RAPHAELITE: Popularly, any modern artist thought to be a would-be restorer of early ideas or methods, as one of the German painters often called Nazarenes, or one who paints and draws with extreme minuteness of detail.
PEDANTY: An assembly or clique of pedants. [Obs.] Milton.
PIGTAIL: 1. The tail of a pig. 2. (Hair Dressing) A cue, or queue. J. & H. Smith. 3. A kind of twisted chewing tobacco. The tobacco he usually cheweth, called pigtail. Swift.
PERITROPAL: 1. Rotatory; circuitous. [R.] 2. Having the axis of the seed perpendicular to the axis of the pericarp to which it is attached.
PEDESTRIOUS: Going on foot; not winged. [Obs.] "Pedestrious animals." Sir T. Browne.
PEDICULATI: An order of fishes including the anglers. See Illust. of Angler and Batfish.
PIERID: Any butterfly of the genus Pieris and related genera. See Cabbage butterfly, under Cabbage.
PASSIVELY: 1. In a passive manner; inertly; unresistingly. 2. As a passive verb; in the passive voice.
PAAGE: A toll for passage over another person's grounds. [Written also peage and pedage.] Burke.
POLYGROOVED: Having many grooves; as, a polygrooved rifle or gun (referring to the rifling).
PREDILECTION: A previous liking; a prepossession of mind in favor of something; predisposition to choose or like; partiality. Burke.
PERSPICIENCE: The act of looking sharply. [Obs.] Bailey.
PERIGASTRIC: Surrounding the stomach; -- applied to the body cavity of Bryozoa and various other Invertebrata.
PHYTOMER: An organic element of a flowering plant; a phyton.
PENTAFID: Divided or cleft into five parts.
PERIBRANCHIAL: Surrounding the branchiæ; as, a peribranchial cavity. Around the bronchi or bronchial tubes; as, the peribronchial lymphatics.
PRONATION: (a) The act of turning the palm or palmar surface of the forefoot downward. (b) That motion of the forearm whereby the palm or palmar, surface is turned downward. (c) The position of the limb resulting from the act of pronation. Opposed to supination.
PRIMINE: The outermost of the two integuments of an ovule. Note: This word has been used by some writers to denote the inner integument, which is formed earlier than the outer. Cf. Secundine.
PACHYDERMATA: A group of hoofed mammals distinguished for the thickness of their skins, including the elephant, hippopotamus, rhinoceros, tapir, horse, and hog. It is now considered an artificial group.
POINTER: One who, or that which, points. Specifically: (a) The hand of a timepiece. (b) (Zoöl.) One of a breed of dogs trained to stop at scent of game, and with the nose point it out to sportsmen. PALEONTOLOGICAL: Of or pertaining to paleontology. -- Pa`le*on`to*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
PHRENOMAGNETISM: The power of exciting the organs of the brain by magnetic or mesmeric influence.
PRANKER: One who dresses showily; a prinker. "A pranker or a dancer." Burton.
PHARO: 1. A pharos; a lighthouse. [Obs.] 2. See Faro.
PHASING TRANSFORMER: Any of several transformers (there must be at least two) for changing phase.
PRECLUSION: The act of precluding, or the state of being precluded; a shutting out.
PAPYREAN: Of or pertaining to papyrus, or to paper; papyraceous.
PROCTORSHIP: The office or dignity of a proctor; also, the term of his office. Clarendon.
POSTHASTE: Haste or speed in traveling, like that of a post or courier. Shak. With speed or expedition; as, he traveled posthaste; to send posthaste. Shak.
PREDICABILITY: The quality or state of being predicable, or affirmable of something, or attributed to something. Reid.
POLARY: Tending to a pole; having a direction toward a pole. [R.] Sir T. Browne.
PERIWIG: A headdress of false hair, usually covering the whole head, and representing the natural hair; a wig. Shak. To dress with a periwig, or with false hair. Swift.
PRIMOGENITURE: 1. The state of being the firstborn of the same parents; seniority by birth among children of the same family. 2. (Eng. PARTICULARITY: 1. The state or quality of being particular; distinctiveness; circumstantiality; minuteness in detail. 2. That which is particular; as: (a) Peculiar quality; individual characteristic; peculiarity. "An old heathen altar with this particularity." Addison. (b) Special circumstance; minute detail; particular. "Even descending to particularities." S...
PERTUSION: The act of punching or piercing with a pointed instrument; as, pertusion of a vein. [R.] Arbuthnot. 2. A punched hole; a perforation. Bacon.
PAYMASTER-GENERAL: 1. (a) (Mil.) In the United States army, an officer of the rank of brigadier general, who commands the pay department, which is charged with the payment of the officers and men. PHLOX: A genus of American herbs, having showy red, white, or purple flowers. Phlox worm (Zoöl.), the larva of an American moth (Heliothis phloxiphaga). It is destructive to phloxes. -- Phlox subulata, the moss pink. See under Moss.
PARA CRESS: An annual asteraceous herb (Spilances oleracea) grown in tropical countries as a pungent salad, and also used medicinally.
PROTEGEE: One under the care and protection of another.
PSALMISTRY: The use of psalms in devotion; psalmody.
PAUROPODA: An order of small myriapods having only nine pairs of legs and destitute of tracheæ.
PREGNABLE: Capable of being entered, taken, or captured; expugnable; as, a pregnable fort. [R.] Cotgrave.
PRIVATEER: 1. An armed private vessel which bears the commission of the sovereign power to cruise against the enemy. See Letters of marque, under Marque. 2. The commander of a privateer. Kidd soon threw off the character of a privateer and became a pirate. Macaulay. To cruise in a privateer.
PSYCHIATRIA: The application of the healing art to mental diseases. Dunglison.
PENTATEUCHAL: Of or pertaining to the Pentateuch.
PRITTLE-PRATTLE: Empty talk; trifling loquacity; prattle; -- used in contempt or ridicule. [Colloq.] Abp. Bramhall.
PHOTOTELESCOPE: A telescope adapted for taking photographs of the heavenly bodies.
PETRESCENT: Petrifying; converting into stone; as, petrescent water. Boyle.
PRIVILY: In a privy manner; privately; secretly. Chaucer. 2 Pet. ii. 1.
PASSIBILITY: The quality or state of being passible; aptness to feel or suffer; sensibility. Hakewill.
PRIMIPARA: A woman who bears a child for the first time.
PARIAL: See Pair royal, under Pair, n.
POSTMASTER: 1. One who has charge of a station for the accommodation of travelers; one who supplies post horses. 2. One who has charge of a post office, and the distribution and forwarding of mails.
PROTECTIVENESS: The quality or state of being protective. W. Pater.
PRETENDERSHIP: The character, right, or claim of a pretender. Swift.
